title: PD-MT244-ProseDiffAnnotations

scope.summary:
GOAL: Let operators and models attach annotations to a PROSE DIFF view. On MT-242's prose diff panel, a reviewer can select a contiguous run of changed blocks (the prose-diff equivalent of a code-diff 'hunk') and attach an annotation whose anchor names the diff side, the block range, and the quoted text; markers and threads reuse the NA family's shared widgets. This closes the prose-diff half of the annotation system: AC MT-201..209 own the schema/anchor/store/routes, NA MT-221/222 render annotations in the code and rich editors, and THIS MT renders them on the block-level prose diff, including model-authored prose-diff annotations.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: NEW module src/frontend/handshake_native/src/annotations/prose_diff_markers.rs (block-range marker placement + anchor construction for the prose diff) registered from src/frontend/handshake_native/src/annotations/mod.rs (the NA family module created in MT-221); marker/selection wiring added to MT-242's prose_diff_ui/panel.rs (the aligned-block accessor MT-242 exposed is the seam); one GUI test file. NO backend edits (consume AC routes via the NA client), NO change to MT-241's engine, NO fork of the NA thread widget.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. HUNK-EQUIVALENT selection: a prose-diff 'hunk' is a maximal contiguous run of non-Unchanged BlockDiff rows (Added/Removed/Modified) in the aligned sequence. Compute these runs from MT-242's aligned block rows; each run is an annotation TARGET. The reviewer can also target a single changed block. Provide a selection affordance on the diff (a gutter/margin marker per hunk plus a click-to-annotate control), reusing the NA marker interaction pattern from MT-221 rather than inventing a new one.
2. ANCHOR construction via AC MT-202: build the annotation anchor as {side: old|new, block range, quoted text}. side = old (left/base) or new (right) per which pane the selected blocks belong to (a Removed run is old-side; an Added run is new-side; a Modified run may carry both — anchor to the NEW side by default and record the paired old-side block range in the anchor's context, never guessing when the side is ambiguous). block range = the half-open aligned block index range of the run mapped to that side's real block indices (from MT-242's row map). quoted text = the concatenated nodeText of the run's blocks on that side (MT-241 already computes per-block text), so the anchor survives later edits via the AC MT-204 re-anchor engine. The AC MT-201 AnnotationSubject for a diff is the Diff{old_ref,new_ref,path} / ProseBlock family — use the diff subject the AC family defines; do NOT invent a new subject shape.
3. MARKERS + THREADS reuse NA widgets: render annotation markers beside each annotated hunk and the inline thread via the SHARED AnnotationThreadWidget from MT-221 (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/annotations/thread_widget.rs) — the same widget MT-222 reuses for the rich editor; do NOT fork it. Marker states (Open/Resolved/Orphaned/Outdated from MT-221's AnnotationMarkerState) apply unchanged; an orphaned prose-diff annotation (its block anchor did not re-resolve) goes to the 'Unanchored annotations' strip pattern MT-221 established, NEVER placed at a guessed block.
4. MODEL-AUTHORED prose-diff annotations: a model reviewing a worktree-merge or notes diff lands its annotations here via the same AC route path the NA client uses; the model provenance badge (robot_id + session id per AC MT-201) renders on the thread exactly as in the code editor. Human and model prose-diff annotations use ONE shared surface (no model-only path).
5. READ vs authoring: this MT renders existing prose-diff annotations and provides the block-range SELECT + attach affordance that constructs the MT-202 anchor and posts through the NA client; the annotation record creation/validation is AC-owned (this MT calls the AC constructor/route, it does not re-implement the schema). Live event-driven arrival and full authoring UX beyond attach follow the NA family's MT-224/225 seams.
6. AccessKit: per-hunk marker `prose_diff_annotation_marker_{side}_{block_start}_{annotation_id}` (Role::Button), the reused thread widget keeps its NA author_ids (`annotation_thread_{annotation_id}` ...), the attach control `prose_diff_annotation_attach_{side}_{block_start}`, all via scoped_author_id and instance-suffixed on the dual-pane side-by-side mount so old/new-side markers never collide.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read AC MT-201 (Annotation record, AnnotationSubject Diff/ProseBlock, provenance), AC MT-202 (the typed AnnotationAnchor: side old|new + block/line range + quoted text + context), NA MT-221 (annotations/mod.rs, marker_state.rs AnnotationMarkerState, thread_widget.rs AnnotationThreadWidget, client.rs NA route consumption, the unanchored strip, the marker interaction + instance-suffix scheme), NA MT-222 (rich-editor reuse of the shared widget), and MT-242 prose_diff_ui/panel.rs (the aligned-block-row accessor + per-block author_ids + old/new indices).
2. Create annotations/prose_diff_markers.rs: compute contiguous changed-block hunks from MT-242's aligned rows; build the MT-202 anchor (side/block range/quoted text) for a selected run; place markers per hunk; route orphaned annotations to the unanchored strip.
3. Wire the selection + attach affordance into prose_diff_ui/panel.rs (using the accessor seam), and mount the shared AnnotationThreadWidget for an opened thread.
4. Ensure model-authored annotations render with the NA provenance badge (robot_id + session id) and share the surface with operator annotations.
5. Register prose_diff_markers in annotations/mod.rs; write the GUI test file (hunk detection, anchor side/range/quoted-text correctness, marker placement in the correct pane, orphaned -> strip, operator vs model badge, dual-mount id non-collision). Capture Argus evidence into HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT.
6. Update the UserManual in the same change (annotating a prose diff: selecting a changed-block run, what the anchor captures, operator vs model annotations, orphaned handling).
allowed_paths: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/annotations/mod.rs (module registration only; owned by NA MT-221)
src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_editor/prose_diff_ui/panel.rs (selection + attach + thread mount wiring via the MT-242 accessor)
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (legacy React; removed by TR MT-261..264)
src/backend/** (annotation core is AC MT-201..209; consume via the NA client/routes only)
acceptance_criteria: A prose-diff 'hunk' (maximal contiguous run of Added/Removed/Modified BlockDiff rows) is computed from MT-242's aligned block rows and is selectable as an annotation target, plus single-changed-block targeting.

The annotation anchor is built via AC MT-202 with side (old|new), the mapped real block-index range for that side, and the concatenated quoted text of the run's blocks; a Modified run anchors to the new side and records the paired old-side range in context, never guessing an ambiguous side.
The annotation record uses the AC MT-201 diff/ProseBlock AnnotationSubject (no new subject shape invented) and is created/posted through the NA client route path, not a re-implemented schema.

Markers and the inline thread reuse the SHARED NA AnnotationThreadWidget (MT-221) unchanged (grep-provable: no second thread-widget struct); marker states (Open/Resolved/Orphaned/Outdated) apply, and an orphaned prose-diff annotation goes to the NA 'Unanchored annotations' strip, never a guessed block.
Model-authored prose-diff annotations land on the SAME surface as operator ones and render the NA model provenance badge (robot_id + session id); no model-only path.

AccessKit: prose_diff_annotation_marker_{side}_{block_start}_{annotation_id} (Button), prose_diff_annotation_attach_{side}_{block_start}, and the reused thread widget's NA author_ids — all via scoped_author_id, instance-suffixed on the side-by-side dual mount so old/new markers never collide.
UserManual updated in the same change: annotating a prose diff, what the anchor captures, operator vs model annotations, orphaned handling.

cargo test -p handshake-native prose_diff_annotations passes; Argus screenshot + AccessKit tree captured for hunk markers (both sides), an open thread with operator+model badges, and the orphaned strip.

! rg -n 'reqwest|axum|struct Annotation ' src/frontend/handshake_native/src/annotations/prose_diff_markers.rs (consumes AC via NA client; no schema fork, no direct route literal)

Argus evidence: argus.screenshot + AccessKit tree dump of (a) hunk markers on old and new sides, (b) an open thread with operator + model provenance badges, (c) an orphaned prose-diff annotation in the unanchored strip — stored under HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT
expected_tests: unit: contiguous changed-block runs computed from aligned rows (single block, multi-block run, two runs separated by unchanged blocks)
unit: anchor construction side/block-range/quoted-text correct for Added (new), Removed (old), Modified (new + paired old context)
integration: SideBySide dual mount places old-side and new-side markers in the correct pane with non-colliding suffixed author_ids
integration: opening a thread mounts the shared NA AnnotationThreadWidget with operator and model badges
integration: an orphaned prose-diff annotation appears in the unanchored strip, never at a body block
negative: a diff with no changed blocks offers no annotation targets
implementation_notes: This MT depends on the NA family surfaces (MT-221 markers/thread widget/unanchored strip/client, MT-222 shared-widget reuse) and the AC anchor model (MT-202 side old|new + range + quoted text; MT-201 Diff/ProseBlock subject + model provenance). Read those contracts before coding; do NOT re-implement the schema, the anchor math, or the thread widget.

The prose-diff 'hunk' is the block-level analogue of a code diff hunk: a contiguous run of changed BlockDiff rows. Compute it from MT-242's aligned-block-row accessor (the seam MT-242 exposes), not by re-diffing.

Side discipline mirrors NA MT-221's merge-pane rule: never place a marker on a guessed side. Removed -> old, Added -> new, Modified -> new with the paired old range recorded in anchor context; if the AC subject cannot name the side, route to the unanchored strip rather than guess.

Model-authored prose-diff annotations use the same AC route + NA client the operator path uses; the single shared surface (human + model) is the whole point of the AC single-schema design — do not add a model-only rendering path.

Cross-family seams (reference only): AC MT-201 record + MT-202 anchor + MT-204 re-anchor verdicts (orphaned/outdated), NA MT-221/222 widgets, MT-242 aligned-block accessor, MT-243 merge conflicts (a later reviewer may annotate merge blocks too). MT-245 does not gate on this MT.

surfaces: prose-diff hunk annotation markers (old and new side)
shared NA AnnotationThreadWidget mounted on the prose diff
unanchored-annotations strip for orphaned prose-diff annotations

target_entries: Annotating a prose diff: selecting a changed-block run (hunk), what the anchor captures (side, block range, quoted text), operator vs model annotations, and orphaned-annotation handling

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Annotation lifecycle FR events are the AC/MT-161 seam; this UI MT renders prose-diff annotations and constructs anchors but emits no new business events beyond the AC create route it calls.
Hunk computation, anchor side/range decisions, and orphan routing are structured/inspectable so a no-context model can diagnose a mis-sided or mis-anchored prose-diff annotation.
Pure render + attach surface; no long-running child process to liveness-track.

risk_if_missed: The prose diff has no annotation surface: a model reviewing a worktree-merge or notes diff cannot leave block-anchored feedback where the change is, operators cannot discuss a specific changed-block run, and prose-diff review falls back to the legacy React editor that TR MT-261..264 removes — leaving the AC/NA annotation system blind to the exact surface (prose diffs) where merge review happens.

risks: RISK-1: Wrong-side anchor — a Removed-block annotation is anchored to the new side (or a Modified run to a guessed side), attaching review commentary to content that does not exist on that side.
RISK-2: Silent misplacement — an orphaned prose-diff annotation (anchor did not re-resolve) is rendered at a guessed block instead of the unanchored strip, attaching feedback to the wrong prose.

RISK-3: Widget fork — a second prose-diff-only thread widget is created instead of reusing the shared NA AnnotationThreadWidget, splitting the annotation surface and drifting behaviour from the code/rich editors.
RISK-4: Provenance laundering — a model-authored prose-diff annotation renders without the robot_id/session badge, reading as operator-authored.
RISK-5: Dual-mount id collision — side-by-side mounts old and new panes; unsuffixed marker ids collide, breaking the Argus/AccessKit path and keyboard access.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): anchor-construction unit tests assert Removed->old, Added->new, Modified->new+paired-old-context; an ambiguous side routes to the unanchored strip, never a guess.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): reuse the NA MT-221 unanchored-strip behaviour; an integration test asserts an orphaned prose-diff annotation appears only in the strip.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): reuse thread_widget.rs unchanged; a grep proof asserts exactly one AnnotationThreadWidget struct in the annotations module.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): the model provenance badge (robot_id + session id) renders for model annotations; a test asserts the badge kind differs by author kind on the prose-diff surface.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): reuse the NA/panel instance-suffix scheme; a dual-mount test asserts non-colliding suffixed marker author_ids for old vs new side.

research_provenance.source: Cross-family contract read 2026-07-21: AC MT-201 (Annotation record, AnnotationSubject Diff{old_ref,new_ref,path}/ProseBlock, model provenance robot_id/session_id/run_id), AC MT-202 (typed AnnotationAnchor side old|new + range + quoted text + context), NA MT-221 (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/annotations/ mod.rs + marker_state.rs AnnotationMarkerState Open/Resolved/Orphaned/Outdated + thread_widget.rs shared AnnotationThreadWidget + client.rs + unanchored strip + marker interaction/instance-suffix scheme), NA MT-222 (shared-widget reuse in the rich editor). Consumes MT-241 per-block nodeText + MT-242 aligned-block-row accessor. Hunk-equivalent concept from code-diff hunk annotations (VS Code Comment API CommentThread(uri,range); hunk noteBorder inline diff annotations) applied at block granularity.
corrections: A prose-diff hunk is a contiguous run of CHANGED BlockDiff rows (block granularity), not a line range; it is computed from MT-242's aligned rows, not re-diffed.

This MT consumes the AC schema/anchor and the NA thread widget; it neither re-implements the annotation record (no `struct Annotation` here) nor forks the thread widget — the single shared human+model surface is preserved.
